preamble: Raising of the nasalized mid back vowel [õ] to [ũ], favoured because nasal coupling blurs perceived vowel height (F1). In Souletin (Zuberoan) Basque, stressed word-final /õ/ regularly raised to /ũ/ (ardũ 'wine' vs. standard ardo), and phonetically nasalized [õ] next to nasal consonants raised sporadically across the eastern dialects (hun 'good' vs. on).

examples.note: Regular raising of stressed word-final /õ/ to /ũ/ in Souletin; likewise arratũ 'rat' (cf. arratoi), arrazũ 'reason' (cf. arrazoi), salũ 'living room' (cf. saloi).
Sporadic raising of phonetically nasalized [õ] beside a nasal consonant, also in hunat 'hither' (cf. hona), kuntü 'account' (cf. kontu); widespread in Souletin and Roncalese.

sources: Egurtzegi, A. (2013). Ekialdeko /o/-ren igoeraren testuinguru fonologikoaren bila / Looking for the phonological context of /o/-raising in Eastern Basque. Anuario del Seminario de Filología Vasca 'Julio de Urquijo' 47(2): 257–266. https://doi.org/10.1387/asju.18683
